Subject: Post-call: SDK auth + embeddings/reranker next steps

Hi Aisha - great call this morning, thanks for walking through Finlytics' reranker plan. Quick recap and immediate next steps so we can get your integration stable:

1) SDK & auth
- We recommend starting with the Redwood JS SDK (attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md).
- Auth options: API key for initial testing; OIDC/JWKS for production. If you want, we can provision a scoped test API key for your eng team.

2) Routing & model choices
- For reranking we suggest rwd-rerank-v1 for quality, and rwd-embed-small as a fallback for heavy throughput.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- For predictable outputs, return a compact JSON schema instead of free text (we can share a schema example).

4) Embeddings / reranker payloads
- Start with small batch sizes (<= 32) and 512-dim vectors. We saw higher memory usage with large batches + long contexts.

5) Debugging / 5xxs
- If you see 5xxs please capture the full curl/request body, timestamp, and any X-Request-ID from response headers. That will expedite a reproduction.

Next steps:
- Please run the attached quickstart and reply with a sample payload and any errors. If you hit a 5xx, include the error_log_20270228.txt and the exact timestamp.
- I'll loop in SE and infra to help triage.

I'll set up a short follow-up once you've tried the quickstart.

Thanks,
Camila

Quick triage notes from SE perspective:
- Repro (local quick test): sending a single request with large context (>1.5MB) + batch >64 caused an upstream timeout in our staging environment.
- Likely causes: oversized payload hitting proxy limits or backend inference host OOMs because of KV cache + large context during reranker embedding step.

Immediate mitigations to ask Finlytics to apply now:
1) Reduce batch size to <= 32 (we saw stable behavior up to 32).
2) Limit context/document sizes to <1MB where possible (truncate/summary beforehand).
3) Set client-side timeout to 60s and enable 3 retries with exponential backoff (jitter).
4) If using SDK, set streaming=false for reranker calls to avoid long-lived streams.

Sample curl we can give them:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-rerank-v1","items":[...max 32 items...],"context":"<truncated_doc>"}' \
  --max-time 60

I attached a small repro script (repro_script.sh) that reproduces the timeout locally against staging and logs request headers (including any X-Request-ID).

- Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: 5xx from Finlytics during reranker test - need triage

I pulled the staging logs and correlated the timestamps from Finlytics' error_log. Observations:
- Backend traces show upstream inference worker hitting a read timeout and OOM when the request included the long context + large batch.
- The reranker flow keeps a KV cache per request which grows with long contexts; combining that with embedding generation for each candidate can spike memory.

Short-term options:
- Route requests with large context to a lower-memory model (rwd-embed-small) as a fallback. We can add routing policy by request size.
- Enforce per-request limits server-side: max_payload_bytes=1048576 (1MB) and batch_limit=32.
- Increase server-side timeout to 90s for large rerank jobs if they must run, but this is a cost trade-off.

Longer-term:
- Ask Finlytics to add a pre-ranking pass that truncates or summarizes documents before reranking.
- We should capture the X-Request-ID from responses (or add it to our gateway) so customers can share it; that accelerates postmortems.

Recommended tunables to pass in SDK headers/params:
- timeout_ms: 90000
- batch_limit: 32
- max_payload_bytes: 1048576
- fallback_model: rwd-embed-small

I
'll open an infra ticket to add routing-by-size policy and request-id headers.

Neha Kapoor | Applied ML / Inference
